description: Section 9.5 steps 10 to 12: a TransactionRecord is evidence that two parties agreed only if its two acts are signed by its two named parties, one each, under different public keys; if the acceptance's signed accepted_offer_id names final_offer.message_id; and if negotiation_summary names the record's initiator and the acceptance's signer. Each record is transaction-record-basis.json's session, one round or two, with acts re-signed by the test-only keys in private_jwks where a case needs it and record_hash resealed, so every check before the one a case targets passes, and in the SAME_SIGNING_KEY cases both signatures genuinely verify. Verify each record with did_documents and the case's offer_hashes; both implementations must reach the stated verdict and expected_reason (null when the record verifies). shape_cases put a value of the wrong type, or no value, in a field these steps read: each is refused, never thrown on, by the reason given. one_round_messages, replayed after transaction-record-basis.json's session_init and session_ack, produce the one_round_control record exactly. spelling_cases bind a DID document to the DID it names (Section 4.2): one party's one document, listing two keys, reaches two spellings of its did:web DID, and the record names one spelling as each party. The document is the document only of the DID its id names, so the other spelling has no document and the record is KEY_NOT_FOUND, never verified; each case's did_documents supplies the document under both spellings. did_syntax_cases hold a party DID to DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: a DID URL (?query, #fragment, /path), a trailing ':', an empty method-specific id, an uppercase method name or scheme, a space, a non-ASCII character or a bad percent-encoding is NOT_BILATERAL; a trailing dot, :path:segments, a %3A port, punycode, '_' and '-' are DIDs, and those records verify. Each case's did_documents names its responder DID exactly.

cases.name: one_round_control
cases.description: A one-round deal: TechCorp (initiator) offers and Acme (responder) accepts. The record the reference implementations generate for it.

cases.name: multi_round_control
cases.description: A two-round deal whose final offer is Acme's (responder) counteroffer, accepted by TechCorp (initiator): transaction-record-basis.json's bound record.

cases.name: offerer_signs_acceptance
cases.description: TechCorp signs the offer and also the acceptance, under its own DID and key; accepting_party_did is TechCorp too. The parties still name Acme as the responder.

cases.name: one_did_for_both_parties
cases.description: parties.responder carries TechCorp's DID and verification method (its organization_name still says Acme Corp), and TechCorp signs both acts.

cases.name: third_party_signs_acceptance
cases.description: The acceptance is signed by did:web:third-party.example with its own valid key, listed in its own DID document; neither party is that DID.

cases.name: one_key_two_spellings
cases.description: parties.responder is did:web:TechCorp.example, a second spelling of the initiator's did:web DID (the host's case differs), with a DID document of its own whose id names that spelling and which lists TechCorp's key. TechCorp's key signs both acts and both signatures verify, so the key comparison is what refuses it. A document that named only one of the spellings would leave the other without a key (spelling_cases).

cases.name: two_dids_one_key
cases.description: parties.responder is did:web:acme-shell.example, a different DID whose document lists TechCorp's key. TechCorp's key signs both acts and both signatures verify.

cases.name: offer_message_id_changed
cases.description: final_offer.message_id, which no signature covers, is changed to name another offer and record_hash is resealed; the acceptance's signed accepted_offer_id still names the original.

cases.name: acceptance_names_another_offer
cases.description: The acceptor signs an acceptance whose accepted_offer_id names the round-1 offer while its accepted_protocol_act_hash is the final offer's.

cases.name: summary_accepting_party_is_offerer
cases.description: negotiation_summary.accepting_party_did, which no signature covers, is set to the offering party (Acme) and record_hash is resealed.

cases.name: summary_initiating_party_is_responder
cases.description: negotiation_summary.initiating_party_did is set to the responder (Acme) and record_hash is resealed.

spelling_cases.name: host_case
spelling_cases.description: One party, one DID document (did:web:techcorp.example) listing key-1 and key-2. The initiator is did:web:techcorp.example and signs the offer with key-1; the responder is did:web:TechCorp.example and signs the acceptance with key-2: the host's case differs; DNS and HTTPS treat the two hosts as one. Both spellings reach the one document, which did_documents supplies under each. Its id names only the first, so the responder has no DID document and its key is unavailable.

spelling_cases.name: trailing_dot
spelling_cases.description: One party, one DID document (did:web:techcorp.example) listing key-1 and key-2. The initiator is did:web:techcorp.example and signs the offer with key-1; the responder is did:web:techcorp.example. and signs the acceptance with key-2: the host carries a trailing dot, the fully qualified spelling of the same name. Both spellings reach the one document, which did_documents supplies under each. Its id names only the first, so the responder has no DID document and its key is unavailable.

spelling_cases.name: percent_encoded_dot
spelling_cases.description: One party, one DID document (did:web:techcorp.example) listing key-1 and key-2. The initiator is did:web:techcorp.example and signs the offer with key-1; the responder is did:web:techcorp%2Eexample and signs the acceptance with key-2: a dot in the host is percent-encoded as %2E. Both spellings reach the one document, which did_documents supplies under each. Its id names only the first, so the responder has no DID document and its key is unavailable.

spelling_cases.name: default_port
spelling_cases.description: One party, one DID document (did:web:techcorp.example) listing key-1 and key-2. The initiator is did:web:techcorp.example and signs the offer with key-1; the responder is did:web:techcorp.example%3A443 and signs the acceptance with key-2: the host states HTTPS's default port, percent-encoded as %3A443. Both spellings reach the one document, which did_documents supplies under each. Its id names only the first, so the responder has no DID document and its key is unavailable.

spelling_cases.name: well_known_path
spelling_cases.description: One party, one DID document (did:web:techcorp.example) listing key-1 and key-2. The initiator is did:web:techcorp.example and signs the offer with key-1; the responder is did:web:techcorp.example:.well-known and signs the acceptance with key-2: a :.well-known path, which did:web maps to the same /.well-known/did.json. Both spellings reach the one document, which did_documents supplies under each. Its id names only the first, so the responder has no DID document and its key is unavailable.

spelling_cases.name: unicode_host
spelling_cases.description: One party, one DID document (did:web:xn--bcher-kva.example) listing key-1 and key-2. The initiator is did:web:xn--bcher-kva.example and signs the offer with key-1; the responder is did:web:bücher.example and signs the acceptance with key-2: the Unicode spelling of a host whose document names its punycode spelling. Both spellings reach the one document, which did_documents supplies under each. Its id names only the first, so the responder has no DID document and its key is unavailable. A raw Unicode host is not DID syntax (DID Core Section 3.1 admits ASCII only), so the record is refused as NOT_BILATERAL before any key is resolved.

did_syntax_cases.name: query
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:techcorp.example?as=acme": a ?query makes it a DID URL, so it is not a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: NOT_BILATERAL. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: fragment
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:techcorp.example#acme": a #fragment makes it a DID URL, so it is not a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: NOT_BILATERAL. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: path
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:techcorp.example/acme": a /path makes it a DID URL, so it is not a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: NOT_BILATERAL. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: trailing_colon
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:techcorp.example:": the method-specific id ends in ':', so it is not a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: NOT_BILATERAL. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: empty_method_specific_id
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:": the method-specific id is empty, so it is not a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: NOT_BILATERAL. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:WEB:techcorp.example": the method name is uppercase, so it is not a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: NOT_BILATERAL. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: uppercase_scheme
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "DID:web:techcorp.example": the scheme is not written 'did', so it is not a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: NOT_BILATERAL. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: space
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:techcorp example": a space is no idchar, so it is not a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: NOT_BILATERAL. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: non_ascii
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:b\u00fccher.example": a non-ASCII character is no idchar, so it is not a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: NOT_BILATERAL. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: bad_percent_encoding
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:techcorp%G1example": '%G1' is not a percent-encoding, so it is not a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax: NOT_BILATERAL. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: trailing_dot
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:techcorp.example.": a trailing dot ('.' is an idchar), so it is a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax, and the record verifies. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:techcorp.example:users:acme": :path:segments, so it is a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax, and the record verifies. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: percent_encoded_port
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:techcorp.example%3A8443": a %3A-encoded port, so it is a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax, and the record verifies. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: punycode
did_syntax_cases.description: parties.responder.did is "did:web:xn--bcher-kva.example": a punycode host, so it is a DID by DID Core Section 3.1's syntax, and the record verifies. The responder's own document names that DID and lists key-2, which signs the acceptance.

did_syntax_cases.name: underscore_and_hyphen
